title: Eddington's eclipse confirms general relativity

tellings.quote: theory and of all people it would take an enemy of Germany um uh Eddington uh to um do the the work on capturing the deviation of a star around the sun during an eclipse

plain: In 1919 the British astronomer Arthur Eddington watched a solar eclipse and measured how starlight bent as it passed the sun, which backed up Albert Einstein's new theory of gravity, called general relativity. A guest named Greg Rogers tells this, noting that "of all people it would take an enemy of Germany" to do the work that proved the German-born physicist right. He tells it to show how science can cross the lines drawn by war.
